transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I keep getting these doubts that I’ve missed something important. Like a number on the mortgage payment, or something in a client proof, or whether a door actually latched. Even after I check, it comes back—like, what if this is the mistake that ruins everything.
Do you find yourself repeating certain actions over and over to try and get rid of these doubts?

Yes… I do. I’ll reopen files, reread emails, check the payment confirmation again. Sometimes I repeat the numbers in my head until they feel right, or settled, I guess. It can make something simple take hours.
Do you feel anxious when these doubts occur?
Yes. I mean… it hits pretty hard. The doubt comes back even after I’ve checked, and then I feel this awful panic, like if I missed one number or one detail, everything could fall apart.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind, beyond just these doubts about making mistakes?

Yes… mostly it’s that same kind of thought, but it repeats. Like, I’ll know I checked the mortgage number or the client proof, or that I shut a door, and then it just barges back in—what if that was the mistake that costs me everything. I don’t really get to just move on from it.
Do you feel like repeating these actions helps reduce your anxiety?

For a little while, yes. Reopening the file or rereading the email makes the panic drop some. Checking the payment confirmation again, or saying the figures in my head until they feel… settled. But it doesn’t really last, and then I can lose hours on something simple.
Are these doubts and repeated actions interfering with your work, relationships, or daily life in any way?

Yes… mostly with work. I’ve missed billable hours, and deadlines get pushed because something that used to take an afternoon can drag on for days now. One client—someone I’ve worked with a long time—has already asked if I can still handle simple revisions on time. That was… hard to hear.
Do you worry about a wide range of everyday things, not just making mistakes?
I don’t think so… not in a general way. It’s mostly tied to whether I’ve done something wrong or missed something important. Everyday things, I guess I worry some, but not like this.
Do you feel like these doubts and the actions you take to try and get rid of them are causing you a lot of distress?

Yes. It’s… upsetting. I keep reopening files or rereading emails, checking payment confirmations, and sometimes I’m just repeating the figures in my head until they feel right. A simple invoice or logo revision can turn into hours I can’t even bill for. So yes, it does distress me.
Do you often find yourself worrying about things in your daily life that aren't related to making mistakes or missing something important?
Not really… I mean, I have normal worries, I suppose, but I haven’t noticed that same kind of worrying unless it’s about having missed something or done something wrong.
How long have you been experiencing these doubts and repeating actions?
I’m not really sure exactly. It’s been… a while, I think. I didn’t really keep track of when it started.
Are these doubts and repeated actions affecting your relationships with family or friends in any way?

A little, I guess. I don’t talk about it much with family or friends, but work has definitely been affected. I’ve missed billable hours and pushed deadlines back because things that used to take an afternoon can drag on for days now. One longtime client even asked if I could still handle simple revisions on time, which was… hard to hear.
Are you avoiding social situations or interactions with family and friends because of these doubts and repeated actions?
I don’t think so… not in any obvious way. I mean, I might keep to myself sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m avoiding people because of it.
Are there any activities or tasks that you're avoiding altogether because of these doubts and fears of making mistakes?
I’m not sure I’d say I’m avoiding anything altogether. I might put some things off, or take longer to start, but… I can’t think of a task I’ve completely stopped doing because of it.
Have you noticed any strain in your personal relationships due to your need to repeat actions or check things multiple times?

Not really personally, no… at least not that I can tell. It’s more that I get stuck with work things — reopening files, rereading emails, checking a payment confirmation, that sort of thing. Sometimes I repeat the numbers in my head until they feel right. It can make a simple invoice or revision take hours, but I don’t usually bring that into relationships much.
Are you feeling like these doubts and repeated actions are affecting your overall quality of life?

Yes… I guess it is. Mostly with work. I’ve missed billable hours, and deadlines have been pushed back because things that used to take me an afternoon can drag on for days now. One longtime client even asked if I could still handle simple revisions on time, which was… hard to hear.
Are there specific tasks or situations that you avoid because of your fear of making mistakes?
I don’t know if I’d call it avoiding, exactly. I hesitate with certain work tasks, especially ones where a small error would matter, but I usually still do them. Just… slowly.
Are you feeling like these doubts and actions are significantly impacting your ability to enjoy your free time or engage in activities you once found pleasurable?

Somewhat, yes. I mean… mostly because work spills over into everything now. I’ve missed billable hours and had to push deadlines back, because things that used to take an afternoon can take days. So by the time I’m done, I don’t really have much energy left for anything else. One longtime client even questioned whether I could still handle simple revisions on time, so… that’s been hard.
Are there any situations or tasks that you're completely avoiding because you're afraid of making a mistake?
Not completely, no. I might put things off or take longer to start, but I don’t think there’s anything I just refuse to do outright.
Do you often worry about things that have nothing to do with making mistakes or missing something important?
Not really… I mean, I’m sure I worry about normal things sometimes, but I haven’t noticed it being a big thing outside of work or checking details.
Are you feeling like these doubts and repeated actions are impacting your relationships with family and friends in a significant way?

Not so much with family and friends, I guess. It’s more… work has been affected. I’ve missed billable hours and had to push deadlines because simple jobs drag on for days now. A longtime client even asked if I could still handle basic revisions on time, which was… embarrassing.
